blind_spots.blind_spot: The chip design process is described entirely in fab/bench-test terms (tape-out, wafer probe, characterization) with no mention of how the resulting ASIC survives the platform's actual power, thermal, and vibration envelope once mounted.
blind_spots.operator_reality: A chip that passes bench characterization in a controlled test rig still has to survive the SWaP-C budget of the actual airframe or sensor pod it ships in; that gap between 'chip works on the bench' and 'chip works in the system' is where many ASIC development programs stall between Phase II and Phase III.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: A 14-person fabless IC house is still in the tape-out/characterization phase of two parallel SBIR Phase IIs, not yet at system integration.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Test System Development: Test bench circuit boards and periphery products to ensure the designed chip technology functions correctly and meets specifications

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Trusted Microelectronics' is marketed as a silicon-level security feature of the chip itself, with no mention anywhere of the company-level CMMC/NIST 800-171 or ITAR compliance a Navy Phase III production award will require.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Tamper-resistance built into an IC doesn't substitute for the company holding CMMC/ITAR compliance as an entity; the Navy won't move controlled defense IP and production dollars to a subcontractor that hasn't cleared that bar, regardless of how secure the chip design is.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Compliance infrastructure is typically the last thing a small engineering-led team builds, and the site's language stays entirely at the product/chip level.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our technology is designed with trust and assurance at their core, ensuring your hardware is secure.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Two SBIR Phase II clocks (Navy MWIR imaging, NASA radiation-hardened LiDAR ASIC) are running in parallel on a 14-person team with no named Phase III transition partner or prime mentioned anywhere.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Phase II funds engineering, not fielding; without an advocacy chain — a program office or prime already committed to carrying the chip into Phase III production — the classic SBIR-mill failure mode is two technically successful Phase IIs and zero fielded programs.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's public materials are entirely engineering-capability focused (what they can design/fab), never acquisition-pathway focused (who takes it to production).
blind_spots.evidence_quote: SenseICs Corporation has been awarded an $850K NASA... SBIR Phase II contract to develop a radiation-hardened FMCW Signal Processing ASIC (FASIC) for next-generation LiDAR sensors.

opener_hook: You're running Navy and NASA SBIR Phase II clocks in parallel on a 14-person team — does either have a named Phase III transition partner yet?
